findings: 7x2 had the smallest isolated stage-2 Q.ANT error (0.02130) but the largest stage-2 input-propagation error (0.09341) and end-to-end error (0.09212).
The amplitude-weighted sensitivity proxy was 0.16507 for 7x2, versus 0.05720 for 14x4 and 0.02540 for 49x2.
The high 7x2 residual is therefore consistent with amplification of upstream perturbations rather than unusually poor isolated Q.ANT approximation in the head.
Across 7x2 seeds, the largest sensitivity proxy coincided with the largest propagation and end-to-end errors.
interpretation: Compatibility depends not only on local accumulation width but also on how strongly downstream learned structure amplifies upstream numerical perturbations.
next_research_direction: Test a predictive model that adds a pre-Q.ANT head-sensitivity feature to stage-1 and stage-2 accumulation counts, with predictions frozen before held-out Q.ANT evaluation.
limitations: The sensitivity measure is a proxy, not a full Jacobian norm.
CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
